### Current Trajectory Average Income at Year 20: $20.5K {#sec-current_trajectory_avg_income_year_20}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Average income (GDP per capita) at year 20 under current trajectory trajectory.

**Inputs**:

- [Current Trajectory GDP at Year 20](#sec-current_trajectory_gdp_year_20) 🔢: $188T
- [Global Population 2045 (Projected)](#sec-global_population_2045_projected) 📊: 9.2 billion of people

$$
\begin{gathered}
\bar{y}_{base,20} \\
= \frac{GDP_{base,20}}{Pop_{2045}} \\
= \frac{\$188T}{9.2B} \\
= \$20.5K
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
GDP_{base,20} = GDP_0(1+g_{base})^{20}
$$
*✓ High confidence*

#### Monte Carlo Distribution

#### Exceedance Probability

:::

### Current Trajectory Cumulative Lifetime Income (Per Capita): $1.18M {#sec-current_trajectory_cumulative_lifetime_income}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Cumulative per-capita income over an average remaining lifespan under current trajectory baseline trajectory. Uses 2.5% baseline growth for all years.

**Inputs**:

- [Global Average Income (2025 Baseline)](#sec-global_avg_income_2025) 🔢: $14.4K
- [Current Trajectory Average Income at Year 20](#sec-current_trajectory_avg_income_year_20) 🔢: $20.5K
- [Baseline Global GDP Growth Rate](#sec-gdp_baseline_growth_rate): 2.5%
- [Average Remaining Years (Median Person)](#sec-global_avg_remaining_years) 🔢: 48.5 years

$$
\begin{gathered}
Y_{cum,earth} \\
= \bar{y}_0 \cdot \frac{(1+g_{base})((1+g_{base})^{T_{remaining}}-1)}{g_{base}}
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

### Years Until Destructive Economy Reaches 25% of GDP: 8 years {#sec-destructive_economy_years_to_25pct_gdp}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Years until the destructive economy (military + cybercrime) reaches 25% of GDP at current growth rates. Historical precedent suggests societies become unstable when extraction rates exceed 20-30% of economic output.

**Inputs**:

- [Destructive Economy as % of GDP](#sec-global_destructive_economy_pct_gdp) 🔢: 11.5%
- [Cybercrime Cost CAGR](#sec-global_cybercrime_cagr) 📊: 15%
- [Military Spending Real CAGR (10-Year)](#sec-global_military_spending_real_cagr_10yr) 📊: 3.4%
- [Baseline Global GDP Growth Rate](#sec-gdp_baseline_growth_rate): 2.5%
- [Global Military Spending in 2024](#sec-global_military_spending_annual_2024) 📊: $2.72T
- [Global Destructive Economy (2025)](#sec-global_destructive_economy_annual_2025) 🔢: $13.2T
- [Global Cybercrime Costs (2025)](#sec-global_cybercrime_cost_annual_2025) 📊: $10.5T

$$
\begin{gathered}
n_{25\%} \\
= \frac{\ln(0.25 / r_{destruct:GDP})}{\ln(1 + g_{destruct} - g_{GDP})}
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Total Annual Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Operational Costs: $40M {#sec-dfda_annual_opex}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Total annual Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment operational costs (sum of all components: platform + staff + infra + regulatory + community)

**Inputs**:

- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Maintenance Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_platform_maintenance): $15M (95% CI: $10M - $22M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Staff Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_staff): $10M (95% CI: $7M - $15M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Infrastructure Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_infrastructure): $8M (95% CI: $5M - $12M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Regulatory Coordination Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_regulatory): $5M (95% CI: $3M - $8M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Community Support Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_community): $2M (95% CI: $1M - $3M)

$$
\begin{gathered}
OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= Cost_{platform} + Cost_{staff} + Cost_{infra} \\
+ Cost_{regulatory} + Cost_{community} \\
= \$15M + \$10M + \$8M + \$5M + \$2M \\
= \$40M
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

### Maximum Trial Capacity Multiplier (Physical Limit): 566x {#sec-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Physical upper bound on trial-capacity multiplier from participant availability. Even with unlimited funding, annual trial enrollment cannot exceed willing participant pool.

**Inputs**:

- [Global Patients Willing to Participate in Clinical Trials](#sec-willing_trial_participants_global) 🔢: 1.08 billion people
- [Annual Global Clinical Trial Participants](#sec-current_trial_slots_available) 📊: 1.9 million patients/year (95% CI: 1.5 million patients/year - 2.3 million patients/year)

$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity,max} \\
= \frac{N_{willing}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{1.08B}{1.9M} \\
= 566
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{willing} \\
= N_{patients} \times Pct_{willing} \\
= 2.4B \times 44.8\% \\
= 1.08B
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

{{< include ../figures/tornado-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical.qmd >}}

{{< include ../figures/sensitivity-table-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical.qmd >}}

#### Monte Carlo Distribution

{{< include ../figures/mc-distribution-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical.qmd >}}

#### Exceedance Probability

{{< include ../figures/exceedance-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical.qmd >}}

:::

### dFDA Patients Fundable Annually: 23.4 million patients/year {#sec-dfda_patients_fundable_annually}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Number of patients fundable annually from dFDA funding at pragmatic trial cost. Source-agnostic counterpart of DIH_PATIENTS_FUNDABLE_ANNUALLY.

**Inputs**:

- [dFDA Annual Trial Subsidies](#sec-dfda_trial_subsidies_annual) 🔢: $21.8B
- [dFDA Pragmatic Trial Cost per Patient](#sec-dfda_pragmatic_trial_cost_per_patient) 📊: $929 (95% CI: $97 - $3K)

$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{fundable,dFDA} \\
= \frac{Subsidies_{dFDA,ann}}{Cost_{pragmatic,pt}} \\
= \frac{\$21.8B}{\$929} \\
= 23.4M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Subsidies_{dFDA,ann} \\
= Funding_{dFDA,ann} - OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= \$21.8B - \$40M \\
= \$21.8B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= Cost_{platform} + Cost_{staff} + Cost_{infra} \\
+ Cost_{regulatory} + Cost_{community} \\
= \$15M + \$10M + \$8M + \$5M + \$2M \\
= \$40M
\end{gathered}
$$
*✓ High confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

### Diseases Without Effective Treatment: 6.65 thousand diseases {#sec-diseases_without_effective_treatment}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Number of diseases without effective treatment. 95% of 7,000 rare diseases lack FDA-approved treatment (per Orphanet 2024). This represents the therapeutic search space that remains unexplored.

$$
\begin{gathered}

= N_{rare} \times 0.95 \\
= 7{,}000 \times 0.95 \\

### Average Remaining Years (Median Person): 48.5 years {#sec-global_avg_remaining_years}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Average remaining lifespan for the median-age person. Conservative: uses life expectancy at birth minus median age, which underestimates remaining years because survivors to age 30 have higher conditional life expectancy.

**Inputs**:

- [Global Life Expectancy (2024)](#sec-global_life_expectancy_2024) 📊: 79 years (SE: ±2 years)
- [Global Median Age (2024)](#sec-global_median_age_2024) 📊: 30.5 years

$$
\begin{gathered}
T_{remaining} \\
= LE_{global} - Age_{median} \\
= 79 - 30.5 \\
= 48.5
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

### Global Destructive Economy (2025): $13.2T {#sec-global_destructive_economy_annual_2025}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Combined annual cost of military spending and cybercrime. The 'destructive economy' that competes with the productive economy.

**Inputs**:

- [Global Military Spending in 2024](#sec-global_military_spending_annual_2024) 📊: $2.72T
- [Global Cybercrime Costs (2025)](#sec-global_cybercrime_cost_annual_2025) 📊: $10.5T

$$
\begin{gathered}
Cost_{destruct} \\
= Spending_{mil} + Cost_{cyber} \\
= \$2.72T + \$10.5T \\
= \$13.2T
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Destructive Economy as % of GDP: 11.5% {#sec-global_destructive_economy_pct_gdp}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Destructive economy (military + cybercrime) as percentage of global GDP.

**Inputs**:

- [Global Destructive Economy (2025)](#sec-global_destructive_economy_annual_2025) 🔢: $13.2T
- [Global GDP (2025)](#sec-global_gdp_2025) 📊: $115T

$$
\begin{gathered}
r_{destruct:GDP} \\
= \frac{Cost_{destruct}}{GDP_{global}} \\
= \frac{\$13.2T}{\$115T} \\
= 11.5\%
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Cost_{destruct} \\
= Spending_{mil} + Cost_{cyber} \\
= \$2.72T + \$10.5T \\
= \$13.2T
\end{gathered}
$$
*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Global Opportunity Cost Total: $101T {#sec-political_dysfunction_global_opportunity_cost_total}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Total global opportunity cost from governance failures: health innovation delays ($34T), underfunded science ($4T), lead poisoning ($6T), migration restrictions ($57T). Sum: $101T annually in unrealized potential.

**Inputs**:

- [Global Health Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_health_opportunity_cost) 📊: $34T (95% CI: $20T - $80T)
- [Global Science Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_science_opportunity_cost) 📊: $4T (95% CI: $2T - $10T)
- [Global Lead Poisoning Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_lead_opportunity_cost) 📊: $6T (95% CI: $4T - $8T)
- [Global Migration Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_migration_opportunity_cost) 📊: $57T (95% CI: $57T - $170T)

$$
\begin{gathered}
O_{total} \\
= O_{health} + O_{science} + O_{lead} + O_{migration} \\
= \$34T + \$4T + \$6T + \$57T \\
= \$101T
\end{gathered}
$$

**Methodology**: [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]

*? Low confidence*

### Percentage Military Spending Cut After WW2: 87.6% {#sec-post_ww2_military_cut_pct}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Percentage US military spending cut after WW2 (1945-1947, inflation-adjusted: $1,420B to $176B in constant 2024 dollars)

**Inputs**:

- [US Military Spending in 1947 (Constant 2024 Dollars)](#sec-us_military_spending_1947_annual_2024usd) 📊: $176B
- [US Military Spending at WW2 Peak (Constant 2024 Dollars)](#sec-us_military_spending_1945_peak_annual_2024usd) 📊: $1.42T

$$
\begin{gathered}
Cut_{WW2} \\
= 1 - \frac{Spending_{US,1947}}{Spending_{US,1945}} \\
= 1 - \frac{\$176B}{\$1.42T} \\
= 87.6\%
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Annual Funding from 1% of Global Military Spending Redirected to DIH: $27.2B {#sec-treaty_annual_funding}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Annual funding from 1% of global military spending redirected to DIH

**Inputs**:

- [Global Military Spending in 2024](#sec-global_military_spending_annual_2024) 📊: $2.72T
- [1% Reduction in Military Spending/War Costs from Treaty](#sec-treaty_reduction_pct): 1%

$$
\begin{gathered}
Funding_{treaty} \\
= Spending_{mil} \times Reduce_{treaty} \\
= \$2.72T \times 1\% \\
= \$27.2B
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Treaty Trajectory Lifetime Income Gain (Per Capita): $14.9M {#sec-treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Lifetime per-capita income gain from Treaty Trajectory vs current trajectory. Cumulative treaty income minus cumulative earth income over average remaining lifespan. Uses global averages; individual gain scales with starting income.

**Inputs**:

- [Treaty Trajectory Cumulative Lifetime Income (Per Capita)](#sec-treaty_trajectory_cumulative_lifetime_income) 🔢: $16.1M
- [Current Trajectory Cumulative Lifetime Income (Per Capita)](#sec-current_trajectory_cumulative_lifetime_income) 🔢: $1.18M

$$
\begin{gathered}
\Delta Y_{lifetime,treaty} \\
= Y_{cum,treaty} - Y_{cum,earth} \\
= \$16.1M - \$1.18M \\
= \$14.9M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Y_{cum,treaty} \\
= \bar{y}_0 \cdot \frac{(1+g_{pc})((1+g_{pc})^{20}-1)}{g_{pc}} \\
+ \bar{y}_{treaty,20} \cdot \frac{(1+g_{base})((1+g_{base})^{T_{remaining}-20}-1)}{g_{base}}
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
\bar{y}_{0} \\
= \frac{GDP_{global}}{Pop_{global}} \\
= \frac{\$115T}{8B} \\
= \$14.4K
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\bar{y}_{treaty,20} = \frac{GDP_{treaty,20}}{Pop_{2045}}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
GDP_{treaty,20} \\
= GDP_0(1+g_{treaty,ramp})^3(1+g_{treaty,full})^{17}
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
s_{mil,max} = Cut_{WW2} = 87.6\% = 87.6\%
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Cut_{WW2} \\
= 1 - \frac{Spending_{US,1947}}{Spending_{US,1945}} \\
= 1 - \frac{\$176B}{\$1.42T} \\
= 87.6\%
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
f_{cure,20,wish} \\
= \min\left(1,\frac{Treatments_{new,ann}\cdot k_{capacity,wish}\cdot 20}{D_{untreated}}\right)
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity} \\
= \frac{N_{fundable,dFDA}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{23.4M}{1.9M} \\
= 12.3
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{fundable,dFDA} \\
= \frac{Subsidies_{dFDA,ann}}{Cost_{pragmatic,pt}} \\
= \frac{\$21.8B}{\$929} \\
= 23.4M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Subsidies_{dFDA,ann} \\
= Funding_{dFDA,ann} - OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= \$21.8B - \$40M \\
= \$21.8B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= Cost_{platform} + Cost_{staff} + Cost_{infra} \\
+ Cost_{regulatory} + Cost_{community} \\
= \$15M + \$10M + \$8M + \$5M + \$2M \\
= \$40M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity,max} \\
= \frac{N_{willing}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{1.08B}{1.9M} \\
= 566
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{willing} \\
= N_{patients} \times Pct_{willing} \\
= 2.4B \times 44.8\% \\
= 1.08B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{untreated} \\
= N_{rare} \times 0.95 \\
= 7{,}000 \times 0.95 \\
= 6{,}650
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
T_{remaining} \\
= LE_{global} - Age_{median} \\
= 79 - 30.5 \\
= 48.5
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Y_{cum,earth} \\
= \bar{y}_0 \cdot \frac{(1+g_{base})((1+g_{base})^{T_{remaining}}-1)}{g_{base}}
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
\bar{y}_{base,20} \\
= \frac{GDP_{base,20}}{Pop_{2045}} \\
= \frac{\$188T}{9.2B} \\
= \$20.5K
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
GDP_{base,20} = GDP_0(1+g_{base})^{20}
$$
*✓ High confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

{{< include ../figures/sensitivity-table-treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita.qmd >}}

### Wishonia Trajectory GDP at Year 20: $10.7 quadrillion {#sec-wishonia_trajectory_gdp_year_20}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Projected global GDP at year 20 under the Wishonia Trajectory. Model applies all Wishonia policy channels and redirects the full Political Dysfunction Tax non-health opportunity pool to highest-marginal-value uses. Health recovery is modeled separately through disease burden removal to avoid overlap. Military and non-health reallocation effects are ramped at 50% intensity for the first 3 years, then 100% for years 4-20, reflecting implementation lag. Military reallocation uses a physically demonstrated upper bound (post-WW2 demobilization) rather than an arbitrary policy cap.

**Inputs**:

- [Global GDP (2025)](#sec-global_gdp_2025) 📊: $115T
- [Baseline Global GDP Growth Rate](#sec-gdp_baseline_growth_rate): 2.5%
- [Wishonia Military Reallocation Physical Max Share](#sec-wishonia_military_reallocation_physical_max_share) 🔢: 87.6%
- [GDP Growth Boost at 30% Military Reallocation](#sec-military_redirect_gdp_boost_at_30pct): 5.5% (95% CI: 3.5% - 7.5%)
- [R&D Spillover Multiplier](#sec-rd_spillover_multiplier): 2x (95% CI: 1.5x - 2.5x)
- [Wishonia Disease Cure Fraction (20yr, Full Implementation)](#sec-wishonia_disease_cure_fraction_20yr_full) 🔢: 100%
- [Disease Burden as % of GDP](#sec-disease_burden_gdp_drag_pct) 📊: 13%
- [Global Science Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_science_opportunity_cost) 📊: $4T (95% CI: $2T - $10T)
- [Global Lead Poisoning Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_lead_opportunity_cost) 📊: $6T (95% CI: $4T - $8T)
- [Global Migration Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_migration_opportunity_cost) 📊: $57T (95% CI: $57T - $170T)
- [Economic Multiplier for Healthcare Investment](#sec-economic_multiplier_healthcare_investment) 📊: 4.3x (95% CI: 3x - 6x)
- [Economic Multiplier for Military Spending](#sec-economic_multiplier_military_spending) 📊: 0.6x (95% CI: 0.4x - 0.9x)

$$
GDP_{wish,20}=GDP_0(1+g_{ramp})^3(1+g_{full})^{17}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

Lifetime per-capita income gain from Wishonia Trajectory vs current trajectory. Cumulative Wishonia income minus cumulative current trajectory income over average remaining lifespan.

**Inputs**:

- [Wishonia Trajectory Cumulative Lifetime Income (Per Capita)](#sec-wishonia_trajectory_cumulative_lifetime_income) 🔢: $53.3M
- [Current Trajectory Cumulative Lifetime Income (Per Capita)](#sec-current_trajectory_cumulative_lifetime_income) 🔢: $1.18M

$$
\begin{gathered}
\Delta Y_{lifetime,wish} \\
= Y_{cum,wish} - Y_{cum,earth} \\
= \$53.3M - \$1.18M \\
= \$52.1M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Y_{cum,wish} \\
= \bar{y}_0 \cdot \frac{(1+g_{pc,wish})((1+g_{pc,wish})^{20}-1)}{g_{pc,wish}} \\
+ \bar{y}_{wish,20} \cdot \frac{(1+g_{base})((1+g_{base})^{T_{remaining}-20}-1)}{g_{base}}
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
\bar{y}_{0} \\
= \frac{GDP_{global}}{Pop_{global}} \\
= \frac{\$115T}{8B} \\
= \$14.4K
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\bar{y}_{wish,20} = \frac{GDP_{wish,20}}{Pop_{2045}}
$$
where:
$$
GDP_{wish,20}=GDP_0(1+g_{ramp})^3(1+g_{full})^{17}
$$
where:
$$
s_{mil,max} = Cut_{WW2} = 87.6\% = 87.6\%
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Cut_{WW2} \\
= 1 - \frac{Spending_{US,1947}}{Spending_{US,1945}} \\
= 1 - \frac{\$176B}{\$1.42T} \\
= 87.6\%
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
f_{cure,20,wish} \\
= \min\left(1,\frac{Treatments_{new,ann}\cdot k_{capacity,wish}\cdot 20}{D_{untreated}}\right)
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity} \\
= \frac{N_{fundable,dFDA}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{23.4M}{1.9M} \\
= 12.3
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{fundable,dFDA} \\
= \frac{Subsidies_{dFDA,ann}}{Cost_{pragmatic,pt}} \\
= \frac{\$21.8B}{\$929} \\
= 23.4M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Subsidies_{dFDA,ann} \\
= Funding_{dFDA,ann} - OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= \$21.8B - \$40M \\
= \$21.8B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
OPEX_{dFDA} \\
= Cost_{platform} + Cost_{staff} + Cost_{infra} \\
+ Cost_{regulatory} + Cost_{community} \\
= \$15M + \$10M + \$8M + \$5M + \$2M \\
= \$40M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity,max} \\
= \frac{N_{willing}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{1.08B}{1.9M} \\
= 566
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{willing} \\
= N_{patients} \times Pct_{willing} \\
= 2.4B \times 44.8\% \\
= 1.08B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{untreated} \\
= N_{rare} \times 0.95 \\
= 7{,}000 \times 0.95 \\
= 6{,}650
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
T_{remaining} \\
= LE_{global} - Age_{median} \\
= 79 - 30.5 \\
= 48.5
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Y_{cum,earth} \\
= \bar{y}_0 \cdot \frac{(1+g_{base})((1+g_{base})^{T_{remaining}}-1)}{g_{base}}
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
\bar{y}_{base,20} \\
= \frac{GDP_{base,20}}{Pop_{2045}} \\
= \frac{\$188T}{9.2B} \\
= \$20.5K
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
GDP_{base,20} = GDP_0(1+g_{base})^{20}
$$
*✓ High confidence*

### Disease Burden as % of GDP: 13% {#sec-disease_burden_gdp_drag_pct}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Fraction of GDP currently lost to disease (productivity losses + medical costs diverted from productive use). $5T productivity loss + $9.9T direct medical costs = $14.9T on $115T GDP = ~13%. As diseases are progressively cured, this drag is recovered as GDP growth. This is the missing factor that makes the treaty trajectory look like a singularity rather than a modest improvement.

**Source**: [@disease-economic-burden-109t]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: Distribution: Fixed

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Global Health Opportunity Cost: $34T {#sec-political_dysfunction_global_health_opportunity_cost}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Annual opportunity cost of slow-motion regulatory environment for health innovation. Murphy-Topel (2006) valued cancer cure at $50T (inflation-adjusted ~$100T in 2025). Longevity dividend of 1 extra year = $38T globally. PCTs could accelerate cures by 10+ years; NPV of 10-year delay at 3% discount = ~$25T. Conservative estimate: $34T annually in lives lost and healthspan denied.

**Source**: [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$20T, $80T] • Distribution: Lognormal (SE: $15T)

### Global Migration Opportunity Cost: $57T {#sec-political_dysfunction_global_migration_opportunity_cost}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Unrealized output from migration restrictions. Clemens (2011) calculated eliminating labor mobility barriers could increase global GDP by 50-150%. At $115T global GDP, lower bound = $57T; upper bound = $170T. Even 5% workforce mobility would generate trillions, exceeding all foreign aid ever given. This is the largest single distortion in the global economy.

**Source**: [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]

#### Uncertainty Range

```{=html}
<script>
// Conservative lazy loading: only load images actually in viewport
(function() {
  'use strict';
  
  let imageObserver = null;
  let loadTimeout = null;
  
  function enableLazyLoading() {
    const images = document.querySelectorAll('img');
    
    // Use Intersection Observer with conservative threshold
    // rootMargin: '50px' means only load images within 50px of viewport
    // This prevents loading images passed through during hash navigation
    imageObserver = new IntersectionObserver((entries, observer) => {
      entries.forEach(entry => {
        if (entry.isIntersecting && entry.intersectionRatio > 0) {
          const img = entry.target;
          // Only load if image is actually visible (not just passed through)
          if (img.dataset.src) {
            img.src = img.dataset.src;
            img.removeAttribute('data-src');
          } else if (!img.hasAttribute('loading')) {
            // For images without data-src, use native lazy loading
            img.setAttribute('loading', 'lazy');
          }
          observer.unobserve(img);
        }
      });
    }, {
      rootMargin: '50px',  // Only load images within 50px of viewport
      threshold: 0.01      // Trigger when at least 1% visible
    });
    
    images.forEach(img => {
      imageObserver.observe(img);
    });
  }
  
  // Handle hash navigation (clicking links to sections)
  // Delay loading to avoid loading images passed through during jump
  function handleHashNavigation() {
    if (loadTimeout) clearTimeout(loadTimeout);
    // Wait 300ms after navigation to let scroll settle
    // Images will load naturally via Intersection Observer when visible
    loadTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
      // Scroll has settled, Intersection Observer will handle visible images
      // No action needed - observer is already watching
    }, 300);
  }
  
  // Initialize on page load
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', enableLazyLoading);
  } else {
    enableLazyLoading();
  }
  
  // Handle hash changes (clicking anchor links)
  window.addEventListener('hashchange', handleHashNavigation);
  
  // Also handle initial hash if page loads with one
  if (window.location.hash) {
    setTimeout(handleHashNavigation, 100);
  }
})();
</script>
```
